sample_unit: benchmark instances (350 per language x 7 languages, MultiMed-X)
languages: seven non-English languages (not named in text)

links.outcome: LLM medical reasoning performance in local languages versus English
links.effect: Reasoning in local languages is substantially weaker than in English; the proposed method improves multilingual reasoning by an average of 5%, with larger gains in low-resource languages.
links.quote: While reasoning-enhanced large language models perform strongly on English medical tasks, a persistent multilingual gap remains, with substantially weaker reasoning in local languages, limiting equitable global medical deployment.

unlisted_practices: Language-informed co-reasoning framework that aligns English and local-language reasoning concepts to reduce multilingual gaps

screen.reason: The study develops a new co-reasoning architecture/framework (Med-CoReasoner) to address multilingual disparity in medical reasoning and benchmarks it on a newly constructed multilingual dataset (MultiMed-X); it evaluates model design rather than an organizational deployment practice.
